stem: Which of the following is a relative contraindication to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use in children?

options.text: Simple viral upper respiratory tract infection

explanation: Severe asthma is a relative contraindication to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug use because NSAIDs can precipitate bronchospasm in susceptible children.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because NSAIDs can precipitate bronchospasm in some children with asthma, so severe asthma is a relative contraindication.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because hypermobility syndrome is not a contraindication to NSAID use and these medicines may be used for associated pain.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because neuropathic pain is not a contraindication to NSAIDs, although they are not usually the main treatment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because NSAIDs are commonly used in palliative care for analgesia and are not contraindicated by the setting alone.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a simple viral upper respiratory tract infection is not a contraindication to NSAID use.

source.hint: Think about a common respiratory condition that might be worsened by certain anti-inflammatory medications.
